title: Rösti
ahead: The day before, boil the potatoes in their skins until a knife meets slight resistance, about 20 min. Drain and refrigerate overnight.
notes: Forgot to boil the potatoes? With 1 h to spare, boil them as usual, halve them and put them in the freezer for 30 min, then follow the recipe. With less time, use them raw: peel, grate and squeeze them very dry in a clean tea towel, without rinsing, then season and shape as usual. Cook over medium-low heat, 15 min covered with a lid, then flip and cook 15 min uncovered. It comes out crunchier and less soft inside.
To make it a full meal, do the optional step: crisp bacon and a fried egg on top of each wedge, never mixed into the potato. Use bacon rather than lardons, which are not good enough in Swiss shops.
Skip the optional step and leave the bacon and eggs off your shopping for a plain side.
Best straight from the pan; the crust softens as it waits.

steps.text: Toss {salt}, some black pepper and {potatoes} gently in a large bowl, just before cooking.
Melt half of {clarified-butter} in a 24 cm non-stick pan over medium heat.
Tip in the potatoes and spread them into an even layer about 2 cm thick. Press down lightly with a spatula.
Cook without stirring until deep golden underneath.
Turn the rösti out onto a large flat plate. Melt the rest of the clarified butter in the pan, then slide the rösti back in, uncooked side down.
Drop {butter} around the edge. Cook until deep golden and crisp.
Optional: meanwhile, fry {bacon} in a second pan until crisp and lift it out. Fry {eggs} in its fat until the whites have set.
Slide onto a warm plate and cut into 4 wedges. Put the bacon and a fried egg on top of each wedge if you made them.
